Subject: Azure Marketplace — legacy subscription consolidation & channel margin implications

Hi Amanda —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Helix is considering consolidating several legacy Azure Marketplace SKUs (three seat-based products + two usage-metered connectors) into a single subscription under a Private Offer so procurement can simplify billing and forecasting. A couple of quick asks from your team we want to address up front:

1) How the Marketplace fee and reseller passback will affect the netback to Helix and any downstream channel partners
2) Whether we can reflect committed discounts for Year 1 on the Private Offer and maintain a static reseller passback schedule
3) Any PO / procurement fields you require in the offer (billing contacts, tax handling, order reference)

Attached: consolidation-pricing-model.xlsx (xlsx) — draft mapping of existing SKUs into proposed package; PO-draft-v1.pdf — sample PO fields we usually surface for private offers.

What we'll do next: Ben is putting together a channel passback proposal (simple tiered percentages) and Grace will prepare a proforma that shows net price after Azure marketplace fee (~3%) and suggested reseller passback. Can you confirm the list of internal approvers for procurement and whether ProcureCo (your reseller) needs line-item evidence for passback calculations?

If it's useful, there is a 30-minute slot on my calendar Monday; here's the link: https://calendly.com/ethan-park/30min

Thanks —

Ethan —

Appreciate the summary and the workbook. A few items from procurement side:

- We need a clear proforma that shows final invoiced amount to Helix and the calculation for reseller passback to ProcureCo. Our finance team requires an example month where usage is pegged to expected run-rate so they can verify netback across the fiscal year.
- ProcureCo (cc'd) will require the passback as either a percentage of list or a fixed fee per-seat; Rajiv, is percentage ok?
- Is Redwood able to commit to keeping the reseller passback percentages unchanged for at least 12 months once the private offer is accepted? We can't go back to 3rd-party distributors during Year 1.

Also: our security/compliance team asked to see an evidence snippet showing where audit logs for usage invoicing will be available — a short note on that in the proforma would help.

We can meet Monday. If you can get the proforma and a simple channel passback table by EOD Monday PT that would put us in good shape for our Tuesday procurement review.

Team —

Attached is a concise channel passback proposal (channel-passback-proposal.csv). Key recommendations based on similar enterprises:

- Enterprise tier (>= $250k ARR): 12% reseller passback, applied against list after marketplace fee.
- Growth tier ($50k–$250k ARR): 9% reseller passback.
- Standard tier (< $50k ARR): 6% reseller passback or $2/seat floor, whichever is higher.

Assumptions & notes:
- Azure marketplace fee estimated 3.0% (marketplace transaction fee). We show netback = list * (1 - marketplace_fee) * (1 - passback%).
- If Helix prefers a fixed-dollar passback we can convert the %s into per-seat or per-connector amounts (Ben can run scenarios).
- We recommend Redwood include a 12-month passback freeze clause in the PO language; ops/legal have approved that as a standard concession for Private Offers.

Action items for Ethan:
1) Confirm which tier Helix expects to land in (we think Enterprise given their current spend but confirm).
2) If they want fixed-dollar passback, say so and we'll convert.
3) Grace/Laura to produce the proforma that includes an example month and the audit log pointer for invoicing evidence.

I kept the messaging consumer-friendly; if you'd like, I can produce two short wording options for the Private Offer (one that references Azure marketplace mechanics explicitly, and one that keeps it high-level for procurement).

Ben Carter

Proforma highlights (see attachment for line-level math):
- List price (pre-marketplace fee): $312,000 / year (consolidated subscription)
- Azure marketplace fee (3.0%): $9,360
- Reseller passback (proposed Enterprise 12% on post-marketplace list): $36,864

Commitments we can include in the Private Offer:

- Audit evidence: Redwood will include a monthly usage statement and a link to invoice-level audit logs (read-only) in the customer console; sample link included in the proforma.
- Conversion option: If Helix prefers a fixed-dollar passback instead of percentage, we can convert the proposed 12% into $/seat or $/connector and update the proforma.

Next steps:

2) Amanda — if this looks ok to submit to finance, we'll finalize the Private Offer language and send the DocuSign link.
3) If procurement wants wording that explicitly references "Azure marketplace fee" or wants that line removed for simplicity, tell us which version you want — we have both.
